images.caption: The City Opera House in Traverse City is a significant building on Front Street in the city's downtown, constructed in 1891 in the Romanesque Revival style, and contained a 1200 seat auditorium for li

brief: A three-storey red-brick commercial block with an ornate pressed-metal cornice lettered 'City Opera House', arched windows and shopfronts with awnings below. One photo. Older than 1970: Petoskey's Gaslight District (the town's model) is a row of 1880-1910 brick commercial blocks; no newer example of this main-street type exists. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the City Opera House (Traverse City MI, 1891): a three-storey red brick front with a central pediment, arcades of arched windows, the name in a stone band; the opera hall upstairs over shops (luggage store, café); street trees

why.note: the opera house over shops: the upper-floor hall paid for by ground-floor rents
